answer.justification: The space posterior to the stomach is the lesser sac (omental bursa). To access this space laparoscopically, the surgeon must enter via the lesser sac by dividing either the gastrohepatic ligament (part of the lesser omentum) or the gastrocolic ligament. Dividing the gastrohepatic ligament provides direct access to the area behind the stomach, which is necessary to reach the pancreas for tumor enucleation.
